title: Trace media recovery across SFU, region, and network failures
description: Follow one direction of a bidirectional call. Select a scenario to see the active media route, failed or degraded scope, recovery assignment, and participant-visible consequence.

nodes.label: Local participants
nodes.detail: Clients encode media layers, report path quality, follow only newer assignment versions, and republish current tracks after transport recovery.

nodes.label: Nearby media edge
nodes.detail: Terminates or steers regional media transport and exposes path plus regional health to the allocator.

nodes.label: Global allocator
nodes.detail: Chooses a healthy region and SFU group from proximity, jurisdiction, assignment version, and reserved recovery headroom.

nodes.label: Primary SFU group
nodes.detail: Receives published layers, keeps ephemeral transport and subscription state, prioritizes audio, and forwards receiver-specific media.

nodes.label: Standby SFU group
nodes.detail: Maintains admission headroom and can accept a newer assignment after a primary SFU process or host failure.

nodes.label: Primary transit path
nodes.detail: Carries media between the active SFU region and remote participants. Loss, jitter, or route inflation can degrade a healthy SFU.

nodes.label: Recovery-region SFU
nodes.detail: Provides independent regional capacity and control dependencies. Its longer route may require an initially conservative video profile.

nodes.label: Remote participants
nodes.detail: Observe freezes, audio gaps, quality changes, and reconnects. Their telemetry confirms whether infrastructure recovery restored the call.

nodes.label: Alternate transit
nodes.detail: Offers an independent path for sustained provider degradation or regional recovery, with its own latency and packet-ordering behavior.

scenarios.label: Healthy nearby route
scenarios.summary: The allocator assigns Region A because it is close and has reserved SFU egress. Media stays on the primary regional and transit path.
scenarios.result: Participants receive the selected layers with the shortest modeled route. The standby SFU and recovery region remain available rather than absorbing normal load to the limit.

scenarios.label: Primary SFU crash
scenarios.summary: The primary SFU loses ephemeral transports and subscriptions. The allocator stops new assignments and issues a higher-version lease for reserved capacity in the same region.
scenarios.result: Clients briefly freeze while reconnecting and republishing to the standby. Meeting identity and roles survive, but media state is rebuilt rather than assumed to be durable.

scenarios.label: Region A outage
scenarios.summary: The nearby edge and both Region A SFU groups are unavailable. The global allocator uses independent Region B capacity and an alternate transit provider.
scenarios.result: The meeting continues under a newer regional assignment, but reconnect time and path latency rise. Start with a conservative video profile, protect audio, and upgrade only after quality stabilizes.

scenarios.label: Transit path degraded
scenarios.summary: Region A and its SFU remain healthy, but sustained loss and route inflation affect the primary transit provider. The media route moves without evacuating the region.
scenarios.result: Participants may see a temporary quality drop or jitter increase during rerouting. Receiver-specific adaptation protects audio while route health is verified and avoids repeated path flapping.
